note: Every sensor is a make target and nothing else. The Makefile is already the single definition of what CI runs (R1.13); binding sensors to it means humans, CI and agents share one vocabulary, and a gate cannot be strengthened in one place and quietly left behind in the others. If a sensor here would need a command that is not a make target, the target is what is missing.

stack.stackNote: The bootstrap scan reported typescript as primary and found no Docker and no build tools. It had indexed experiments/ and the browser SDK only — the Go service under services/ingestion/internal was absent from its map entirely. Corrected by hand rather than preserved: a harness that describes the wrong repository is worse than none.

sensors.name: gofmt clean
sensors.description: Every Go source is gofmt -s clean. Formatting is never litigated in review here.

sensors.name: race suite
sensors.description: go test -race across both modules. The api package drives real HTTP rather than calling handlers directly, because v1 lost a provenance chain to a field-name mismatch that every in-memory test survived.

sensors.name: golangci-lint
sensors.description: Core defect-class set only (.golangci.yml). Every linter guards a class of bug, not a preference — a config that fires on style teaches people to read red as noise.

sensors.name: govulncheck
sensors.description: Reachable advisories in both modules. go.mod pins toolchain go1.26.5 as the security floor.

sensors.name: generated artifacts match their sources
sensors.description: libs/genproto from schemas/, contract/openapi.yaml from the Go wire types, contract/fixtures/ from the harness wire modules. All three are committed and drift-gated; none may be edited by hand.

sensors.name: OpenAPI specification lint
sensors.description: Curated vacuum ruleset (.vacuum.yaml), failing on warnings. It has already caught a schema demanding every field of a discriminated union, and a published example outside its own enumeration.

sensors.name: experiment harness syntax and asserted selftests
sensors.description: py_compile, node --check, the statistics selftest (22 assertions) and the numbers-schema fixture corpus (21 fixtures). No browsers, no network — the part of the harness that is checkable on every push.

sensors.name: go.mod tidy
sensors.description: Runs against copies and restores the originals, so the check never mutates the tree it is judging.

sensors.name: coverage measured
sensors.description: Reported, never thresholded. -coverpkg so the wire-level tests get credit for the packages they actually drive. A threshold would become a number to satisfy; this figure exists to be looked at.

sensors.name: the whole gate
sensors.description: Everything CI runs, in the order CI runs it. `make ci` green locally and a green pipeline are the same statement — that equivalence is the reason the Makefile exists.

sensors.name: the six numbers
sensors.description: THE project invariant, and deliberately outside `make ci`: it needs real browsers and takes about seven minutes. Required after any change touching services/, experiments/ or schemas/. The target now MEASURES AND CHECKS: it compares the run against the newest manifest in docs/results/ and fails on a rate outside the baseline's Wilson interval in either direction, a tier that has gone missing, p99 over the 80ms budget, a cold start that blocks, a false-positive rate that lost its value, or a >10% memory regression. The comparison logic is itself asserted by experiments-check, inside `make ci`, where it needs no browsers. Tiers 5 and 6 are seeded (GT_SEED), so their figures are repeatable; a moved number with no explanation is indistinguishable from a broken detector.
